scope_limit_declared_up_front.statement: The scenario's input tuple (attacker, level, roster, build, fight window) is NOT reachable from the permitted evidence tree — golden scenario definitions live under scripts/, which this runbook forbids. data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json does not contain 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster', and no file under data/ names it.
scope_limit_declared_up_front.consequence: The computation below is a RELATIVE (ratio-level) recomputation plus a two-sided bound, not an absolute recomputation of total_damage from champion base stats. Every step is still derived from cached wiki text and quoted formulas; the conclusion is therefore sound but is a bound-and-match argument rather than a from-scratch number.
searches_run_to_try_to_locate_the_scenar: data/bin/characters/* is gitignored (README states 17 MB regenerable), so the game-file numeric layer is unavailable in the export

sources_quoted.text: Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.
Non-{{tip|basic damage}} dealt on the same target may apply stacks only once per frame.

After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

sources_quoted.where: data/items.json — corroborating usages that fix the {{rd|melee|ranged}} argument order
sources_quoted.text: Blade of the Ruined King {{rd|9%|6%}} (Mist's Edge: 9% melee / 6% ranged), Ravenous Hydra {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}} (Cleave: 40% melee / 20% ranged), Divine Sunderer {{rd|6%|4%}}. => Expose Weakness is 8% for a melee holder, 5% for a ranged holder.
m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)  (apply_resistance, resistance.py); post = raw · m(R)  <=>  raw = post · (1 + R/100)
the mitigation operator x -> x·100/(100+R) is *linear in raw damage* for a fixed resistance

Black Cleaver average stacks (ArmorReductionEffect.average_reduction): the established model uses a fixed 0.8·max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch) ... the exact Cesàro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C − C(C−1)/(2h) for h >= C

sources_quoted.where: data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json (fight-window vocabulary of this engine's corpora)
sources_quoted.text: "fight": "one_rotation" | "time_based" | "time_based_10s" — i.e. there is a default timed window plus an explicitly-named 10 s variant.

step_1_exact_delta.rounding_band_on_the_ratio: leaf values are carried to 1 dp, so the true ratio lies in [288.25/277.25, 288.35/277.15] = [1.0396754, 1.0404113]
step_1_exact_delta.conclusion: the change is a clean multiplicative +4.00% on this source: 277.2 × 1.04 = 288.288 -> 288.3 (1 dp). 1.04 is the only 'round' ratio inside the band.

hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness.rule: S3 + S4: the target takes 8% (melee holder) / 5% (ranged holder) increased damage from ALL sources for 4 s after the empowered attack.
hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness.windowing: an amp that covers a fraction f of the source's damage events multiplies the source total by (1 + a·f) — exact, because mitigation is linear in raw damage (S6), so the amp commutes with mitigation and with the per-hit sum.
solutions_that_do_not_match: melee amp over a 10 s window (f = 0.4): 286.07 -> 286.1;  ranged over 10 s: 282.74 -> 282.7  (NOT 288.3)
hypothesis_A_bloodsong_expose_weakness.verdict_on_A: The new value sits strictly between 'amp absent' (277.2) and 'amp applied to the whole fight' (291.1 ranged / 299.4 melee), which is exactly and only where a correctly time-windowed application of the sourced 4 s Expose Weakness debuff can land. Both natural window fractions (4 s of a 5 s default timed fight at the ranged 5%, or 4 s of an 8 s fight at the melee 8%) reproduce 288.3 to the last displayed digit. The old value 277.2 equals the amp-free total, i.e. it prices the Bloodsong debuff at zero — which contradicts S3's 'increased damage from all sources'.

hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_stack_model.rule: S1 + S7: Carve caps at 5 stacks × 6% = 30% armor reduction; the engine's documented approximation uses 0.8·max_stacks = 4 stacks = 24% reduction, and the doc recommends the exact Cesàro mean C − C(C−1)/(2h) = 5 − 10/h.
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_stack_model.test: with post-penetration armor R, a stack change s_old=4 -> s_new multiplies damage by (100 + 0.76R)/(100 + (1 − 0.06·s_new)R). Setting this to 1.0400 gives: s_new = 5.0 requires R = 125.00 exactly; s_new = 4.8 requires R = 204.9; s_new = 4.5 requires R = 5000.
hypothesis_B_black_cleaver_stack_model.verdict_on_B: Rejected as the explanation. (i) The exact Cesàro mean is 5 − 10/h < 5 for any finite hit count, so it can never reach the s_new = 5 that a 4% bump would need at a plausible armor value. (ii) Every other s_new demands an implausible, hand-picked armor (205, 5000). (iii) A 6-stack cap (which would fit R ≈ 205) directly contradicts the cached wiki text S1 ('stacking up to 5 times ... up to 30% at 5 stacks'). Hypothesis B can only produce +4.00% by coincidence; hypothesis A produces it from the item's own printed numbers.

hypothesis_C_both_wrong.test: For 'both wrong' to hold, the true value would have to be neither the amp-free total nor the windowed-amp total. The two-sided bound from S3 pins the true value into (277.2, 299.4] for a melee holder and (277.2, 291.1] for a ranged holder, and any correct engine that authors the debuff on a timeline lands at 277.2·(1 + a·f) for the scenario's own f. 288.3 is the value for the two natural f; 277.2 is the value for f = 0, i.e. for the debuff not existing.
hypothesis_C_both_wrong.verdict_on_C: Not supported: 277.2 is a boundary of the admissible interval and is excluded by S3; 288.3 is interior and reconstructible from the printed numbers.

independent_computation.step_3_direction_check: Both mechanics named in the scenario id are strictly damage-INCREASING debuffs on the target — Carve removes armor (S1, raising m(R) = 100/(100+R) per S5) and Expose Weakness amplifies all incoming damage (S3). A fix that makes the coupled roster price a previously-unpriced target debuff must move this leaf UP. The observed change is upward, of exactly the magnitude the printed 4 s / 5%–8% debuff supports.
independent_computation.residual_uncertainty: I could not read the scenario's roster to determine whether the Bloodsong holder is melee (8%) or ranged (5%), nor the fight window length; both admissible pairings ((5%, 4 s of 5 s) and (8%, 4 s of 8 s)) give the same 288.3, so the verdict does not depend on resolving it. What I cannot rule out from data/ alone is a wrong pairing that coincidentally also yields 1.04 (e.g. melee 8% mis-priced over a window that is really 5 s long, which would want 277.2 × 1.064 = 294.9 -> 294.9, not 288.3 — so this specific mis-pairing is in fact excluded).

confidence: medium-high. The +4.00% delta is reconstructed exactly from the cached Bloodsong text (S3) under either admissible melee/ranged pairing, and the old value is excluded because it prices a printed 'increased damage from all sources' debuff at zero. Confidence is not 'high' only because the scenario input tuple is outside the permitted evidence tree, so this is a ratio-and-bounds proof rather than an absolute recomputation.
verdict_statement: new_value_correct — 288.3 is the value the cached wiki text supports; 277.2 corresponds to the sourced Expose Weakness amplification being priced at zero.
